name: Abū Muḥammad Yaḥyā ibn al-Mubārak al-ʿAdawī al-Yazīdī
summary: Basran reader and grammarian who handed on Abū ʿAmr's reading of the Qurʾān, tutored the caliph al-Maʾmūn and was al-Kisāʾī's rival at the ʿAbbāsid court.
bio: Al-Yazīdī took his name from Yazīd ibn Manṣūr, maternal uncle of the caliph al-Mahdī, whose sons he taught. He was the main student of Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ in the reading of the Qurʾān, and the two transmitters of that reading still recited today, al-Dūrī and al-Sūsī, took it from him. In grammar he learnt from Abū ʿAmr and al-Khalīl and stood, in al-Zubaydī, in the sixth Basran generation with Sībawayh.

In Baghdad he tutored al-Maʾmūn, while al-Kisāʾī tutored al-Amīn, and the sources tell of the debates between the two teachers at court. He died in Merv in 202/817, said to be over seventy. His sons and grandsons were scholars after him, and al-Zubaydī gives three of them entries of their own.
